'''Charles Ehresmann''' (19 April 1905 – 22 September 1979) was a German-born French [[mathematician]] who worked in [[differential topology]] and [[category theory]].

He was an early member of the [[Bourbaki group]], and is known for his work on the differential geometry of smooth [[fiber bundle]]s, notably the introduction of the concepts of [[Ehresmann connection]] and of [[jet bundle]]s, and for his seminar on category theory.

==Life==

Ehresmann was born in [[Strasbourg]] (at the time part of the [[German Empire]]) to an [[Alsatian language|Alsatian]]-speaking family; his father was a gardener. After [[World War I]], [[Alsace]] returned part of [[French Third Republic|France]] and Ehresmann was taught in French at [[Lycée Kléber]].<ref name=":2">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Ehresmann}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Dieudonné |first=Jean |author-link=Jean Dieudonné |date=2007 |title=Ehresmann, Charles |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/science/dictionaries-thesauruses-pictures-and-press-releases/ehresmann-charles |access-date=2022-02-18 |website=[[Complete Dictionary of Scientific Biography]] |publisher=[[Charles Scribner's Sons]]}}</ref>

Between 1924 and 1927 he studied at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] (ENS) in Paris and obtained [[agrégation]] in mathematics. After one year of military service, in 1928-29 he taught at a French school in [[Rabat]], Morocco. He studied further at the [[University of Göttingen]] during the years 1930–31, and at [[Princeton University]] in 1932–34.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />

He completed his [[Thesis|PhD thesis]] entitled ''Sur la topologie de certains espaces homogènes'' (On the topology of certain [[homogeneous space]]s) at ENS in 1934 under the supervision of [[Élie Cartan]].<ref name=":0">{{MathGenealogy|id=96080}}</ref>

From 1935 to 1939 he was a researcher with the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] and he contributed to the [[French mathematical seminars|seminar]] of [[Gaston Julia]], which was a forerunner of the [[Bourbaki seminar]]. In 1939 Ehresmann became a lecturer at the [[University of Strasbourg]], but one year later the whole faculty was evacuated to [[Clermont-Ferrand]] due to the [[German occupation of France]]. When Germany withdrew in 1945, he returned to Strasbourg.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />

From 1955 he was Professor of Topology at [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]], and after it split into multiple universities in 1969 he ended up at [[Paris Diderot University]] (Paris 7).

Ehresmann was President of the [[Société Mathématique de France]] in 1965.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liste anciens présidents {{!}} Société Mathématique de France |url=https://smf.emath.fr/la-smf/les-presidents-de-la-smf-depuis-1873 |access-date=2022-02-18 |website=smf.emath.fr}}</ref> He was awarded in 1940 the [[Prix Francoeur]] for young researchers in mathematics<ref>{{Cite web |title=Charles Ehresmann |url=http://serge.mehl.free.fr/chrono/Ehresmann.html |access-date=2022-02-18 |website=serge.mehl.free.fr |language=fr}}</ref> and in 1967 an [[Honorary Doctorate|honorary doctorate]] by the [[University of Bologna]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lauree Honoris Causa – Archivio Storico |url=https://archiviostorico.unibo.it/it/patrimonio-documentario/lauree-honoris-causa/?record=112749 |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=archiviostorico.unibo.it |language=it}}</ref> He also held visiting chairs at [[Yale University]], [[Princeton University]], in Brazil ([[São Paulo]], [[Rio de Janeiro]]), [[Buenos Aires]], Mexico City, [[Montreal]], and the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] in [[Mumbai|Bombay]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CTHS – EHRESMANN Charles |url=https://cths.fr/an/savant.php?id=112708# |access-date=2022-02-18 |website=cths.fr}}</ref>

After his retirement in 1975 and until 1978 he gave lectures at the [[University of Picardy Jules Verne|University of Picardy]] at [[Amiens]], where he moved because his second wife, [[Andrée Charles-Ehresmann]], was a professor of mathematics there. He died at Amiens in 1979.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />

== Mathematical work ==

In the first part of his career Ehresmann introduced many new mathematical objects in [[differential geometry]] and [[Differential topology|topology]], which gave rise to entire new fields, often developed later by his students.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Libermann |first=Paulette |author-link=Paulette Libermann |date=2007 |title=Charles Ehresmann's concepts in differential geometry |url=http://journals.impan.pl/cgi-bin/doi?bc76-0-2 |journal=Geometry and Topology of Manifolds |series=Banach Center Publications |volume=76 |language=en |location=Będlewo, Poland |publisher=Institute of Mathematics Polish Academy of Sciences |pages=35–50 |doi=10.4064/bc76-0-2|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Andrée C. |author-link=Andrée Ehresmann |date=2007 |title=How Charles Ehresmann's vision of geometry developed with time |url=http://journals.impan.pl/cgi-bin/doi?bc76-0-1 |journal=Geometry and Topology of Manifolds |series=Banach Center Publications |volume=76 |language=en |location=Będlewo, Poland |publisher=Institute of Mathematics Polish Academy of Sciences |pages=29–34 |doi=10.4064/bc76-0-1|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":1" />

In his first works he investigated the topology and homology of manifolds associated with classical [[Lie groups]], such as [[Grassmannian|Grassmann manifolds]] and other [[homogeneous space]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |date=1934 |title=Sur la Topologie de Certains Espaces Homogenes |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1968440 |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=35 |issue=2 |pages=396–443 |doi=10.2307/1968440 |jstor=1968440 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |date=1936 |title=Sur les espaces localement homogènes |trans-title=On locally homogeneous spaces |url=https://zbmath.org/?q=an%3A62.1473.03 |journal=Enseign. Math. |language=fr |volume=35 |pages=317–333 |jfm=62.1473.03}}</ref>

He developed the concept of [[fiber bundle]], and the related notions of [[Ehresmann connection]] and [[solder form]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Marle |first=Charles-Michel |author-link=Charles-Michel Marle |date=2007 |title=The works of Charles Ehresmann on connections: from Cartan connections to connections on fibre bundles |url=http://journals.impan.pl/cgi-bin/doi?bc76-0-4 |journal=Geometry and Topology of Manifolds |series=Banach Center Publications |volume=76 |language=en |location=Będlewo, Poland |publisher=Institute of Mathematics Polish Academy of Sciences |pages=65–86 |doi=10.4064/bc76-0-4|s2cid=43455645 |doi-access=free |arxiv=1401.8272 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |date=1947 |title=Sur les espaces fibrés différentiables |trans-title=On differentiable fibred bundles |url=https://zbmath.org/?q=an:0029.42001 |journal=[[Comptes rendus de l'Académie des Sciences]] |language=fr |volume=224 |pages=1611–1612 |zbl=0029.42001}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |date=1949 |title=Sur la théorie des espaces fibres |trans-title=On the theory of fibred bundles |url=https://zbmath.org/?q=an:0039.39703 |journal=Colloques Internat. Centre Nat. Rech. Sci. (Topologie Algebrique) |language=fr |volume=12 |pages=3–15 |zbl=0039.39703}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |date=1955 |title=Les prolongements d'un espace fibré différentiable |trans-title=The prolongations of a differentiable fibred bundle |journal=[[Comptes rendus de l'Académie des Sciences]] |language=fr |volume=240 |pages=1755–1757}}</ref> building on the works by [[Herbert Seifert]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Seifert |first=Herbert |date=1933 |title=Topologie Dreidimensionaler Gefaserter Räume |trans-title=Topology of tridimensional fibred space |url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.acta/1485887992 |journal=Acta Mathematica |language=de |volume=60 |pages=147–238 |doi=10.1007/BF02398271 |s2cid=122571694 |issn=0001-5962 |via=[[Project Euclid]]|doi-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[Hassler Whitney]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Whitney |first=Hassler |date=1935-07-01 |title=Sphere-Spaces |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |language=en |volume=21 |issue=7 |pages=464–468 |doi=10.1073/pnas.21.7.464 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=1076627 |pmid=16588001|bibcode=1935PNAS...21..464W |doi-access=free }}</ref> in the 1930s. [[Norman Steenrod]] was working in the same direction from a topological point of view,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Steenrod |first=Norman |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9781400883875/html |title=The Topology of Fibre Bundles. (PMS-14), Volume 14 |publisher=Princeton University Press |year=1951 |language=en |doi=10.1515/9781400883875 |author-link=Norman Steenrod}} {{isbn|978-1-4008-8387-5  }}.</ref> but Ehresmann, influenced by Cartan's ideas, was particularly interested in differentiable (smooth) fiber bundles, and in the differential-geometric aspects of these.<ref name=":1" /> This approach led him also to the notion of [[Almost-complex structure|almost complex structure]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |date=1952 |title=Sur les variétés presques complexes |trans-title=On almost complex manifolds |url=https://zbmath.org/?q=an%3A0049.12904 |journal=Proc. Internat. Congr. Math. |language=fr |volume=2 |pages=412–419 |zbl=0049.12904}}</ref> which was introduced independently also by [[Heinz Hopf]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hopf |first=Heinz |author-link=Heinz Hopf |date=1948 |title=Zur Topologie der komplexen Mannigfaltigkeiten |trans-title=On the topology of complex manifolds |journal=Studies and Essays Presented to R. Courant on His 60th Birthday |language=de |publication-place=New York |pages=167–185}}</ref>

In order to obtain a more conceptual understanding of completely integrable systems of [[partial differential equation]]s, in 1944 Ehresmann inaugurated the theory of [[foliation]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Haefliger |first=André |author-link=André Haefliger |date=2005 |title=Naissance des feuilletages, d'Ehresmann-Reeb à Novikov |trans-title=Birth of foliations, from Ehresmann-Reeb to Novikov |journal=Géométrie au XXe Siècle, 1930-2000: Histoire et Horizons |language=fr |publisher=Hermann |pages=257–272}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |author-link=Charles Ehresmann |date=1951 |title=Sur la théorie des variétés feuilletées |trans-title=On the theory of foliated manifolds |journal=[[Rendiconti di Matematica e delle sue Applicazioni]] |language=fr |publisher=[[Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica Francesco Severi|Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica]] |publication-place=Rome |volume=10 |issue=5 |pages=64–82}}</ref> which will be later developed by his student [[Georges Reeb]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Reeb |first=Georges |author-link=Georges Reeb |date=1952 |title=Sur certaines propriétés topologiques des variétés feuilletées |trans-title=On certain topological properties of foliated manifolds |url=https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb32560469t |journal=Actualités Scientifiques et Industrielles |language=fr |publisher=Hermann |publication-place=Paris |volume=1183 |pages=5–89, 155–156 |mr=0055692}}</ref> With the same perspective, he pioneered the notions of [[Jet (mathematics)|jet]] and of [[Lie groupoid]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pradines |first=Jean |date=2007 |title=In Ehresmann's footsteps: from group geometries to groupoid geometries |url=http://journals.impan.pl/cgi-bin/doi?bc76-0-5 |journal=Geometry and Topology of Manifolds |series=Banach Center Publications |volume=76 |language=en |location=Będlewo, Poland |publisher=Institute of Mathematics Polish Academy of Sciences |pages=87–157 |doi=10.4064/bc76-0-5|arxiv=0711.1608 |s2cid=17743849 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tulczyjew |first=Włodzimierz M. |date=2007 |title=Evolution of Eresmann's jet theory |url=http://journals.impan.pl/cgi-bin/doi?bc76-0-6 |journal=Geometry and Topology of Manifolds |series=Banach Center Publications |volume=76 |language=en |location=Będlewo, Poland |publisher=Institute of Mathematics Polish Academy of Sciences |pages=159–176 |doi=10.4064/bc76-0-6|s2cid=17456748 |doi-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |author-link=Charles Ehresmann |date=1959 |title=Catégories topologiques et categories différentiables |trans-title=Topological categories and differentiable categories |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/files/EhresmannCategoriesTopologiques.pdf |journal=Colloque de Géométrie différentielle globale |language=French |publisher=CBRM, Bruxelles |pages=137–150}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |author-link=Charles Ehresmann |date=1963 |title=Catégories structurées |trans-title=Structured categories |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=ASENS_1963_3_80_4_349_0 |journal=Annales scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure |language=fr |volume=80 |issue=4 |pages=349–426 |doi=10.24033/asens.1125 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Since the 1960s, Ehresmann's research interests moved to [[category theory]], where he introduced the concepts of [[Sketch (mathematics)|sketch]], of [[multiplicative graph]], and of [[strict 2-category]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ehresmann |first=Charles |date=1968 |title=Esquisses et types des structures algébriques |trans-title=Sketches and types of algebraic structures |url=https://zbmath.org/?q=an%3A0049.12904 |journal=Bul. Inst. Politeh. Iaşi |series=New Series |language=fr |volume=14 |issue=18 |pages=1–14 |mr=0238918 |zbl=0196.03102}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ehresmann |first1=Charles |last2=Bastiani |first2=Andrée |author-link2=Andrée Ehresmann |date=1972 |title=Categories of sketched structures |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=CTGDC_1972__13_2_104_0 |journal=[[Cahiers de Topologie et Géométrie Différentielle Catégoriques]] |language=en |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=105–214 |zbl=0263.18009}}</ref>

His collected works, edited by his wife, appeared in seven volumes in 1980–1983 (four volumes published by Imprimerie Evrard, Amiens, and the rest in the journal ''[[Cahiers de Topologie et Géométrie Différentielle Catégoriques]]'', which he had founded in 1957).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Oeuvres de Charles Ehresmann|url=https://ehres.pagesperso-orange.fr/C.E.WORKS_fichiers/C.E_Works.htm|access-date=2022-02-18|website=ehres.pagesperso-orange.fr}}</ref> His publications include also the books ''Catégories et structures'' (Dunod, Paris, 1965) and ''Algèbre'' (1969).

[[Jean Dieudonné]] described Ehresmann's personality as "''... distinguished by forthrightness, simplicity, and total absence of conceit or careerism. As a teacher he was outstanding, not so much for the brilliance of his lectures as for the inspiration and tireless guidance he generously gave to his research students ... ''"<ref name=":1" />

He had 76 PhD students, including [[Georges Reeb]], [[Wu Wenjun]] (吴文俊), [[André Haefliger]], [[Valentin Poénaru]], and Daniel Tanré.<ref name=":0" /> His first student was [[Jacques Feldbau]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Audin|first=Michèle|author-link=Michèle Audin|date=2009|title=Publier sous l'Occupation. Autour du cas de Jacques Feldbau et de l'Académie des Sciences|trans-title=Publish under the Occupation. On the case of Jacques Feldbau and the Academy of Sciences|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/RHM_2009__15_1_7_0/|journal=Revue d'histoire des mathématiques|language=fr|volume=15|issue=1|pages=7–57}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Audin|first=Michèle|author-link=Michèle Audin|date=March 2008|title=Differential Geometry, Strasbourg, 1953|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200803/tx080300366p.pdf|journal=[[Notices of the AMS]]|volume=55|pages=366–370}}</ref>
